title: Modelled ozone anomalies did not decrease next-year butterfly population growth on 2,844 UK transects in 1990-2023; a northern negative link followed site trends shared with NO2
abstract: We tested if high growing-season ozone at a site decreases butterfly population growth to the next year. We used 360,709 year-to-year changes of UK Butterfly Monitoring Scheme site indices (2,844 transects, 60 species, 1990-2023) and April-September ozone from the EMEP MSC-W model (0.1 degree, rv5.6). Models used site-by-species and species-by-year fixed effects, so the ozone slope came only from spatial ozone differences within a year. They also controlled for E-OBS temperature, rain and radiation, nitrogen deposition and density. In the pre-specified primary test, 1 SD (1.04 ppm h) more AOT40 gave 0.30% lower next-year growth (95% CI -1.48% to +0.88%; year-permutation p = 0.45). Legume-feeding species, whose host plants are ozone-sensitive, did not have more negative slopes (difference from grass feeders +2.25, SE 1.38, x100 log units). A stomatal-flux measure (POD1) gave a small negative slope (-0.70, SE 0.32) that did not stay with an NO2 control (-0.26). Mean-ozone anomalies had r = -0.93 with NO2 anomalies, and their negative slope changed sign with an NO2 control. Outside southern England the AOT40 slope was -3.92 (SE 1.15), but ozone from two years later gave the same slope, and the slope went to zero or positive with NO2 control or site trends; thus, it followed shared long-term site trends, not ozone timing. Limitations: exposure is model output; only 13% of AOT40 variance is within site and year; the design cannot test effects of the national ozone decrease; the planned WCBS replication was not possible.

display.caption: Slope of next-year butterfly growth on the ozone anomaly (x100 log units per 1 SD). Blue: estimate and 95% CI (SE clustered by year). Grey: central 95% of slopes with year-permuted ozone maps. a: pre-specified and robustness models for all UKBMS transects. b: exploratory checks of the negative slope outside southern England. The placebo with ozone two years later gives the same slope, and NO2 control or site trends remove it.
Ozone (AOT40) slopes for 37 butterfly species with 1,500 or more growth pairs, by main larval host group. Lines are 95% CIs (SE clustered by year). Legume feeders do not have more negative slopes.

a: mean April-September AOT40 (EMEP rv5.6) at the 2,844 UKBMS transects, 1990-2023. b, c: AOT40 anomalies after removal of site and year means for 2006 and 2018, in SD units. The test uses only these within-year spatial differences.
